episodes.title: Typing In Copy
episodes.text: You arrive and sit down at your computer. You open the layout for your supervisor. You key in the client copy word by word.

episodes.title: Sizing Type and Pictures
episodes.text: You look at the illustration and the block of copy together. You decide how big each should be and where they sit. You pick the style and size of the type to fit.

trial.title: Set the page parts
items: Select the size of type
Arrange the copy around the illustration
Select the style of type
Set the size of the illustration
trial.explain: You size the picture first, then place copy and pick type to fit it.

episodes.title: Logo Layout Options
episodes.text: You work on sample layouts for a company logo. You try two different concepts using the same layout principles. You wait to see which direction holds up.

choice.prompt: You have time to develop one logo layout further before lunch. Which do you work up?

options.label: Develop the simpler product illustration layout
options.outcome: You build out the simple version. It is clean and ready to show after lunch.

options.label: Develop the busier website header layout
options.outcome: You build out the busy version. It takes longer and still feels crowded.

episodes.title: Same Keys Again
episodes.text: You sit back at your computer after lunch. You key in the same kind of copy corrections as yesterday. You do it again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Last Check Problem
episodes.text: You open the final layout before it goes to the client.

choice.prompt: You see a spacing error in the final layout. What do you do?

options.label: Flag it and suggest a fix now
options.outcome: You pause the send and note the fix. The layout goes out late but correct.

options.label: Send it as is
options.outcome: You send the layout on time. The error goes to the client with it.

chat.text: Is that final layout ready to send?
Look close at the last page before you say yes.

episodes.title: Sample Concepts Done
episodes.text: You go back to your sample layouts. You shape a few concepts into finished designs. You leave them ready for review in the morning.

episodes.title: Planning Morning Sets
episodes.text: You sit at the front desk before anyone arrives. You look over who is signed up and what they can handle. You pick movements for each muscle set and match music to the pace.

trial.title: Order your planning steps
items: Pick music to match the pace of each set
Put the warm-up, sets, and cool-down in order
Check what the group can and cannot do today
List a different movement for each muscle set
trial.explain: You check capabilities first, then movements, then music, then the full order.

episodes.title: First New Assessment
episodes.text: You meet a new person on the mat. You ask about past injuries and watch how they move. You write a short starting program that fits what you see.

episodes.title: Watching the Floor
episodes.text: You walk the room during the set. A regular in the back row is arching hard on every rep.

choice.prompt: She is mid-set and looking at you. Do you correct her now?

options.label: Stop and show the fix now
options.outcome: You pause her, show a smaller range, and she finishes the set without the pinch.

options.label: Let her finish the set
options.outcome: She finishes with the same arch. You pull her aside after and walk through the fix.

options.label: Offer her the easier version
options.outcome: You swap her to the bent-knee version and stay close for two reps until it steadies.

chat.text: Does this look right? My lower back feels pinched.
I was trying to keep up with the front row.

episodes.title: Same Midday Class
episodes.text: You run the same noon class as yesterday. You call out the same easier and harder versions at the same spots. Same as tomorrow.

episodes.title: Checking Progress Notes
episodes.text: You pull out your notebook between sessions. You compare last week's reps to this week's. You change two programs slightly for next week.

episodes.title: Knees Cave In
episodes.text: You watch the evening group start squats. One man's knees cave in every time and he does not notice.

choice.prompt: He keeps going with wobbly knees. What do you do?

options.label: Stop him and fix stance
options.outcome: You stop the set, reset his feet, and have him do three slow reps to hold the line.

options.label: Switch him to the supported option
options.outcome: You move him to the chair-assisted squat and his knees track steady for the rest.

chat.text: Are my knees supposed to feel like this?
They feel wobbly coming up.

episodes.title: Wiping Down Stations
episodes.text: You arrive and pull on your smock. You wipe down your station and the chair arms. You wash the combs and scissors in sanitizer and lay them out. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Morning Appointment Book
episodes.text: You sit down with the appointment book. You call back two clients to schedule their fittings. You update their customer records with the services they had last time.

trial.title: Booking the visit
trial.says: Can I come in tomorrow afternoon for a fitting?
options: Maybe, we're pretty busy, you'll have to see.
Yes, I can schedule you tomorrow afternoon — what time works for you?
Just walk in sometime and we'll fit you in.
trial.explain: You offer a clear time and schedule the appointment.

episodes.title: First Wig Trim
episodes.text: You settle your client in the chair and check her hairpiece against her face. She explains how short she wants the sides. You pick up your scissors and start trimming to shape it.

choice.prompt: She wants it shorter on one side than you think suits her face. What do you do?

options.label: Cut exactly what she asked for
options.outcome: You trim it exactly as she asked. She sees the uneven length in the mirror and asks you to fix it.

options.label: Stop and check with her first
options.outcome: You hold up the hairpiece and show her the length. She nods and agrees to a more even trim.

episodes.title: Color Touch-Up
episodes.text: You mix the tint and brush it onto the hairpiece with the applicator. You work it through section by section. You set a timer and watch the color develop.

episodes.title: Talking Through the Fit
episodes.text: Your next client is unsure about the shape for his hairpiece.

chat.text: I told them last time I wanted it shorter on top.
But it still feels too full on the sides for my face.
Can you shape it different today?

episodes.title: Color Lifting Fast
episodes.text: You check the bleach on a hairpiece and it is lifting faster than expected. The ends look much lighter than the roots. You need to act now before it over-processes.

choice.prompt: The bleach is getting too light on the ends. What do you do?

options.label: Rinse the bleach out now
options.outcome: You rinse the hairpiece right away. The color stops lifting and you can even it out after.

options.label: Leave it to finish the time
options.outcome: You leave it a few more minutes. The ends turn brittle and overly light.

options.label: Wipe one test strand and recheck
options.outcome: You wipe a small strand to check the true lift. You see it is ready and you rinse it out.

episodes.title: Morning Belt Check
episodes.text: You arrive at the small shop and open the side panel on the blower motor. You run it slow and watch the belt, drive, and motor for wear. You check the fluid level and wipe dust off the filter housing.

trial.title: Spot what needs attention
trial.scenario: The motor runs but squeals. The belt edge is frayed and shiny. The fluid level is full and the housing is clean.
options: Frayed belt on the motor drive
Full fluid reservoir
Clean filter housing
trial.explain: The frayed belt is the only wear that needs attention first.

episodes.title: Filter Round Again
episodes.text: You walk the same route you walked yesterday. You check fluid levels, swap out filters, and write down the readings. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Leveling The Unit
episodes.text: You set your level across the top of the pump unit. You loosen the base bolts with a hand wrench and tap the corner true. You check it again with the straightedge until it sits flat.

episodes.title: The Noisy Press
episodes.text: You stand by the press with the owner while it rattles through a cycle.

choice.prompt: The press clanks on each cycle. Do you shut it down to test it now or let it run until Friday?

options.label: Shut it down and test now
options.outcome: You stop the press and run it empty. You find the loose drive part and show the owner.

options.label: Let it run until Friday
options.outcome: You leave it running and note the noise location. You come back Friday to inspect it again.

chat.text: It started clanking this morning. Can you tell what it is?
Should we keep running it until Friday?

episodes.title: Motor Stops Cold
episodes.text: The exhaust fan motor quits in the middle of the afternoon. You test power to it and find the motor is dead. You pull your wrenches and hoist to get it out for repair.

choice.prompt: The fan motor is dead and the shop is getting hot. Do you repair it now or swap in a temporary fix?

options.label: Repair it now with tools on hand
options.outcome: You stay late with hammers, wrenches, and testers. The fan runs again before you leave.

options.label: Lock it out and come back
options.outcome: You tag it out and leave the fan off. The shop stays warm until you return with parts.

options.label: Call for a replacement motor
options.outcome: You call the supplier and wait for a motor. You install it when it arrives.

episodes.title: Ordering Replacement Parts
episodes.text: You sit down at the desk with your worn parts list. You look through the supplier catalog for belts and filters. You place the order for what you used today.

episodes.title: Checking Filters Again
episodes.text: You arrive at the same building as yesterday. You check fluid levels, look over belts and motors, and replace a dirty filter. Same checks again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Testing The Noisy Motor
episodes.text: You stand beside the motor that has been humming wrong. You operate it, listen, and watch how it runs. You test it again to pin down the malfunction.

episodes.title: Straightening The Control Arm
episodes.text: You set your level against the control arm and see it sits low. You loosen it with a hand tool and shift it true. You check it again with a straightedge.

trial.title: Line up the part
items: Tighten the part back down with a hand tool
Check the alignment with a level
Shift the part until it sits true
Confirm it with a straightedge
trial.explain: You check first, then move it, confirm it, and tighten it last.

episodes.title: Motor Stops Midday
episodes.text: You hear the machine shut down mid-cycle. You open the housing and find a loose drive and a worn belt.

choice.prompt: The drive is loose and the belt is worn. What do you do first?

options.label: Secure the drive and repair what you can now
options.outcome: You tighten the drive with wrenches and refit the belt. The machine runs, but the worn belt still needs replacing soon.

options.label: Shut it down and order a new belt
options.outcome: You lock out the machine and leave it off. It stays down until the new belt arrives and you return to fit it.

chat.text: It just quit on us. Can you look at it now?
We need it back today if we can.

episodes.title: Repairing The Drive Assembly
episodes.text: You pull your wrenches and drill to work on the drive assembly. You refit the loose parts and repair the worn mounting. You run the machine to confirm the fix holds.

choice.prompt: The mounting is cracked but holding after your fix. How do you leave it?

options.label: Reinforce the repair now
options.outcome: You spend another hour bracing and tightening the assembly. It runs steady and you note it for the next maintenance check.

options.label: Leave it running and watch it
options.outcome: You keep the machine running and recheck the repair twice. It holds, and you plan to revisit it on the next visit.

episodes.title: Ordering New Belts
episodes.text: You sit down with your supplier catalog at the end of the day. You pick out the right belts and filters for stock. You place the order for delivery.

episodes.title: Reading Charts Before Boarding
episodes.text: You arrive at the pilot station before sunrise. You sit down with maps, charts, and the weather report. You mark water depths, tides, and currents for the morning move.

episodes.title: Holding Steady in Channel
episodes.text: You stand the long run up the marked channel. You watch the buoys, depth finder, and radar tick past. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Calling Out Course Change
episodes.text: You ride beside the captain on the bridge. You call the course and speed for the bend against the tide. The wind is pushing the bow off.

choice.prompt: The wind builds on the bow in the turn — what do you order?

options.label: Slow down and hold center
options.outcome: You slow. The ship stays in deep water but the wind pushes the bow wide and the turn takes longer.

options.label: Add speed to hold heading
options.outcome: You add speed. The rudder bites better and she holds the ordered course through the bend.

episodes.title: Stopping an Unsafe Pass
episodes.text: A small craft cuts toward the channel right ahead of you. You see the distance close too fast for a safe pass.

choice.prompt: The channel ahead is no longer clear — what do you do?

options.label: Stop the ship and wait
options.outcome: You stop and hold position. The small craft clears and you resume when the channel is safe.

options.label: Sound and try to pass around
options.outcome: You sound and try to edge past. The space stays tight and you must stop anyway to avoid a close pass.

options.label: Call the other craft on radio to clear
options.outcome: You call on the radio and direct it clear. It alters course and you proceed once the way is safe.

chat.text: Pilot, can we still come through? We are on schedule.
Tug alongside — that runner is closing on our bow.
What do you want us to do?

episodes.title: Docking at the Berth
episodes.text: You take over as docking master off the berth. You judge wind and current against the pier. You ease her sideways to the berth with the tugs.

trial.title: Check the Approach
trial.scenario: You are coming to the berth with a crosswind pushing you off. The sounder shows shallow water under the keel. A buoy light ahead is dark.
options: Hold for the wind set before giving sideways way
Ignore the sounder and go faster
Steer straight for the dark buoy
trial.explain: You must allow for wind and guard depth before closing the berth.

episodes.title: Steering Out Past Buoys
episodes.text: You take her back out in fading light. You steer by radar, buoys, and the lighthouse lights. You call positions on the radio as you go.

episodes.title: Building The Containment
episodes.text: You arrive at the old boiler room and pull on your coveralls. You carry in plastic sheeting and tape the walls shut. You seal the door flap for the abatement work ahead.

episodes.title: Checking For Hazards
episodes.text: You walk the room with a monitoring device in your hand. You sweep it slowly over pipes and wall patches. You mark where it signals asbestos and lead.

trial.title: Find what needs attention
trial.scenario: You sweep the monitor over three pipe joints. Two read clear. One keeps beeping and flashing over the insulation.
options: The joint that keeps beeping
A joint that read clear
The clean floor nearby
trial.explain: You mark and remove only where the monitor shows hazardous material.

episodes.title: Scraping Pipes Clean
episodes.text: You stand inside the containment in your mask. You scrape asbestos off the pipe with a hand scraper. You vacuum the loose fibers as you work.

choice.prompt: The scraper is slow on a thick patch. Do you switch to the power tool or keep scraping by hand?

options.label: Switch to the power vacuum attachment
options.outcome: You swap tools and clear the thick patch faster. You vacuum again to catch the extra dust.

options.label: Keep scraping by hand
options.outcome: You stay with the hand scraper and work the patch off in strips. It takes longer but the area stays clean.

episodes.title: Bagging The Same Waste
episodes.text: You fold and seal waste bags for storage. You label each one and stack it by the wall. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Alarm During Removal
episodes.text: You are spraying a wall section when your monitor starts beeping fast.

choice.prompt: Your monitor keeps alarming inside containment. What do you do?

options.label: Stop work and back out
options.outcome: You set down the sprayer and step out. You reseal the flap and wait for the air check.

options.label: Keep spraying to finish fast
options.outcome: You finish the patch but dust builds up inside. You still have to stop and reseal after.

chat.text: Stop what you are doing.
What is your monitor showing?
Back out of containment and reseal it.

episodes.title: Counting Stored Drums
episodes.text: You walk the row of sealed drums at the disposal area. You count each container and note the waste type. You hand in the tally for the day.

episodes.title: Morning Care Data
episodes.text: You sit down and open today's nursing care list. You identify which patient data you need for nursing care. You collect it into one place for review.

episodes.title: Nurses and Engineers
episodes.text: You join an online call with nurses and an engineer to talk through one nursing step.

choice.prompt: The nurses describe the check one way and the model shows it another way. What do you do first?

options.label: Redraw the model with the nurses
options.outcome: You update the object model together on the call. The engineer sees the missing step and adds it.

options.label: Ask nurses to follow the model
options.outcome: You stay on the call while they try it. The missing step still causes confusion in the chart.

options.label: Pause and review notes separately
options.outcome: You end the call and compare both versions side by side. You bring a revised model to the next call.

chat.text: We check the wound the same way each shift, it is not in your model.
Can you show us how you chart that check now?

episodes.title: Fixing the Form
episodes.text: You look at a health record screen that confuses nurses during charting. You use informatics ideas to sketch a simpler way to enter the same care information. You share the draft for testing.

trial.title: Order the data work
items: Record the nursing care data
Analyze the nursing care data
Identify the data relevant to nursing care
Collect the data relevant to nursing care
trial.explain: You first identify what you need, then collect it, record it, and analyze it.

episodes.title: Same Charting Again
episodes.text: You sit back down to record the same nursing care data fields. You enter them line by line as yesterday. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Privacy Flag
episodes.text: You notice patient information is visible to staff who do not need it. You stop and check who can see what. You need to protect the privacy of that information now.

choice.prompt: Extra staff can see private patient notes. What do you do?

options.label: Limit access right away
options.outcome: You change the access so only needed staff see the notes. You note the change for policy review.

options.label: Leave access and report later
options.outcome: You keep access as is and send a note for later review. The notes stay visible until someone changes them.

episodes.title: Reviewing the Numbers
episodes.text: You look over patient and nursing data from this week. You analyze patterns to see where nursing services slow down. You note one clear idea to improve care.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Healthcare Administrator — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: People need things from you — questions, help, decisions. You deal with them one at a time, the way this job always does. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: Someone you're working with asks you to take on one more thing — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you today.

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Tools-and-systems time: you work the equipment and the screens of the trade until the thing in front of you does what it should. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Morning Safety Brief
episodes.text: You arrive at the site and join the crew by the trailer. You listen to the morning safety regulations for today's work area. You walk your assigned ground and look for marked hazards.

episodes.title: Checking Fuel Levels
episodes.text: You walk to the fuel supply tanks with the gauge. You check each tank the same way as yesterday, same as tomorrow. You put the caps back and head to your machine.

episodes.title: Starting the Bulldozer
episodes.text: You climb into the bulldozer and sit down in the seat. You start the engine and move the throttle and levers. You press the pedals and ease the machine forward.

choice.prompt: The engine is running but the throttle feels slow to respond. What do you do?

options.label: Stay parked and recheck the controls
options.outcome: You stay parked and work the throttle and switches again. The engine steadies and you start work a few minutes late.

options.label: Ease forward slowly anyway
options.outcome: You ease forward slowly and the machine stays sluggish. You stop and wait for the mechanic to take a look.

episodes.title: Following Hand Signals
episodes.text: You sit in the backhoe with your hands on the levers. You watch your crew member for hand signals. You position the load and move it only when he signals.

trial.title: Move on signal
items: Move the load as the signal directs
Stop and wait for the next signal
Watch the crew member for a hand signal
Position the machine for the load
trial.explain: You watch first, then position, then move, then stop.

episodes.title: Utility Line Warning
episodes.text: You are grading near the north edge when your spotter waves you down. You stop the machine and stay in the seat.

choice.prompt: You are stopped right by a possible utility line. What do you do?

options.label: Stay stopped and wait for direction
options.outcome: You keep the machine still with the engine idling. The crew marks the line and guides you around it.

options.label: Back up a little to give space
options.outcome: You ease back a few feet to clear the marker. You wait there until the crew confirms the safe path.

options.label: Shut down where you are
options.outcome: You shut the engine down and stay in the cab. The crew comes to you and talks through the next move.

chat.text: Stop! Stop! Utility line marker right ahead.
You are close to it with the blade.
Hold there. Do not move until we mark it clear.

episodes.title: Final Walk Around
episodes.text: You park the machine and shut off the engine. You step down and check the area is clear of other workers and gear. You follow the safety path back toward the gate.

episodes.title: Morning Walkaround Check
episodes.text: You arrive in the early light and pull out the pre-flight checklist. You walk around the aircraft and look for defects and malfunctions. You check each item off as you go.

episodes.title: Takeoff With Your Crew
episodes.text: You sit down with the other crew member and talk through the takeoff plan. You agree on who does what for takeoff and landing. You strap in and start the engines together.

choice.prompt: You and your crew member disagree slightly on the timing for takeoff. What do you do?

options.label: Pause and confirm the takeoff steps together
options.outcome: You talk it through and agree on each step. You start the takeoff together with no confusion.

options.label: Go ahead on your own timing
options.outcome: You start moving while your crew member is still getting ready. You have to stop and reset the takeoff.

episodes.title: Flying Blind On Instruments
episodes.text: You fly on into low cloud and the visibility drops away. You keep your eyes on the instruments to guide the flight. You hold to the flight plan and steady the controls.

trial.title: What Needs Attention First
trial.scenario: You are guiding the flight on instruments in poor visibility. One instrument shows you drifting off the planned course, while the cabin mail bag has shifted slightly.
options: Re-secure the mail bag first
Correct back to the planned course on instruments
Log the flight time first
trial.explain: Staying on the flight plan on instruments comes first when visibility is poor.

episodes.title: Holding Steady Course
episodes.text: You sit at the controls and hold the aircraft to the flight plan. You follow the same regulations and procedures as yesterday. It is the same checks again, and it will be the same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Warning Light In Flight
episodes.text: You see a warning light and feel a malfunction in flight.

choice.prompt: The malfunction warning stays on. What do you do first?

options.label: Follow the emergency procedure and report it
options.outcome: You work the steps with your crew and call it in. You stabilize the aircraft and report the malfunction.

options.label: Wait and see if the warning clears
options.outcome: You keep flying and watch the light stay on. The malfunction continues and you still have to respond.

options.label: Hand full control to the other crew member
options.outcome: You step back without briefing the handover. The response is delayed while you sort out who is flying.

chat.text: I see the warning too. Engine readings look wrong.
Want me to read the emergency steps out loud?
I am ready when you are.

episodes.title: Writing Up The Flight
episodes.text: You sit down after landing and report the in-flight malfunction. You write what happened and what you did about it. You file the report with the flight records.

episodes.title: Pouring Wax Blocks
episodes.text: You arrive in the cool lab and pull up the day's tissue cassettes. You sit down at the embedding station and orient each tissue in warm paraffin wax. You press the blocks to chill and check that each one is firm and flat.

episodes.title: Cutting Thin Sections
episodes.text: You sit down at the microtome with your chilled wax blocks. You clamp in a block and cut thin sections of tissue for microscopic examination. You float the ribbon on the water bath and pick up the best sections.

trial.title: Find the bad section
trial.scenario: You cut three sections of body tissue for microscopic examination. Two sections are smooth and whole. One section is torn and bunched up.
options: The torn section
The smooth whole sections
The empty glass slides
trial.explain: The torn section will not show cell details clearly under the microscope.

episodes.title: Staining Slides
episodes.text: You stand at the staining bench with another full rack of slides. You dip them through dyes and chemicals, tray after tray. Same colors, same order as yesterday, same again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Slides for Pathologist
episodes.text: You gather slides at your bench to compile the case for the pathologist.

choice.prompt: One requisition is missing from the tray. What do you do before you send it?

options.label: Send what you have now
options.outcome: The pathologist starts without the requisition and has to stop to ask you for it.

options.label: Stop and find the requisition
options.outcome: You add the missing requisition and hand over slides, draft, and paperwork together.

chat.text: Do you have the slides and requisition for this morning's case?
I also need the surgical working draft with it.

episodes.title: Microtome Stops Mid-Cut
episodes.text: You are cutting sections for microscopic examination when the microtome blade drags and tears. The sections come out thick and scored, no good for the microscope. More blocks are waiting and the staining rack is filling.

choice.prompt: The sections are unusable. What do you do next?

options.label: Keep cutting and staining
options.outcome: You stain torn sections. The cell details stay hidden and you have to recut them.

options.label: Pause and check the blade and block
options.outcome: You reset the block and change the blade, then cut clean sections for staining.

options.label: Move on to the next block
options.outcome: You leave the bad block aside and keep cutting. You come back to it later.

episodes.title: Logging Maintenance Checks
episodes.text: You sit down with the logbook at the end of the day. You compile records of preventive maintenance and instrument performance checks. You date each entry and file it by schedule and regulation.

episodes.title: Morning Getting Up
episodes.text: You arrive and say good morning. You help her sit up on the edge of the bed. You stay close while she stands and help her dress and comb her hair.

choice.prompt: She feels tired and wants to lie back down. Do you let her rest or keep going?

options.label: Take it slow and keep helping up
options.outcome: You wait, then help her stand and finish dressing. She moves slowly but starts the day.

options.label: Let her lie back down for now
options.outcome: You help her lie back and cover her. You come back in a little while to try again.

episodes.title: Time For Bath
episodes.text: You walk with him to the bathroom. You check the water and help him into the bath. You help him wash and then dry off safely.

trial.title: Bathing in order
items: Help the patient wash safely in the bath
Lay out towels and clean clothes nearby
Dry the patient and help out of the bath
Check the water and help the patient in
trial.explain: You set out what you need before the water and washing start.

episodes.title: Sheets and Laundry
episodes.text: You strip the bed and put on clean linens. You gather the laundry and start the wash. You wipe down the room and fold what is dry. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Midday Medicines
episodes.text: You bring out the pill box for lunch time.

chat.text: Do I have to take these now?
I feel fine today.
Can it wait till later?

episodes.title: Unsteady On Feet
episodes.text: You help him move from the wheelchair to the bed. Halfway up his legs wobble and he grips your arm hard. You hold him steady and ease him back into the chair.

choice.prompt: He is pale and unsteady. What do you do next?

options.label: Keep him seated and call the nurse
options.outcome: You keep him in the chair and call the nurse to report what you saw. You stay with him until she tells you what to do.

options.label: Try the move again right away
options.outcome: You wait a minute and try to lift him again. He is still shaky and you settle him back down.

options.label: Let him walk alone to rest
options.outcome: You step back and he tries to stand on his own. He sways and has to sit down again.

episodes.title: Writing The Notes
episodes.text: You sit down with your notebook. You write what care you gave and how each patient did today. You list the bath, the medicines, and the trouble standing.

episodes.title: Morning Plan Review
episodes.text: You arrive at the office and unroll the house plans on your desk. You sit down and read the blueprints against the code book. You mark where the layout meets safety rules.

episodes.title: Checking Outlet Wiring
episodes.text: You stand in the same model unit as yesterday and watch the outlet wiring go in. You check each box the same way you always do. Same checklist tomorrow.

episodes.title: Explaining a Permit
episodes.text: A builder waits at the counter to ask about his occupancy permit.

choice.prompt: He wants to move in before the permit is ready. What do you do?

options.label: Hold the permit until it passes
options.outcome: You explain what still needs to pass. He leaves with a clear list and a later date.

options.label: Issue a partial move-in note
options.outcome: You check the rules and find you cannot do that. You have to hold the permit anyway.

chat.text: Can I move in this weekend if the last inspection is close?
Remember, occupancy needs full compliance first.
So what do I need to do?

episodes.title: Foundation Walkthrough
episodes.text: You walk the foundation of a new build after the pour. You look at the concrete and the grading for cracks and fit. You compare what you see to the specifications.

trial.title: Spot the problem first
trial.scenario: You are inspecting a foundation after construction. The walls look straight and the grading slopes away. One section of wiring in the crawlspace is exposed and hot to the touch.
options: Exposed live wiring in the crawlspace
Straight foundation walls
Grading that slopes away
trial.explain: Exposed live wiring is the immediate safety risk.

episodes.title: Unsafe Wiring Found
episodes.text: You are on site watching a water heater hookup when you see the wiring is wrong.

choice.prompt: The installer wants to turn the power on to test it. What do you do?

options.label: Stop the test and require a fix
options.outcome: You stop the power-up. The installer shuts it down and redoes the wiring to code.

options.label: Let him test it briefly
options.outcome: You stay and watch, then shut it down when it sparks. You require a full redo before anyone continues.

chat.text: Looks like they crossed the circuits to save time.
Do not let them power that up.

episodes.title: Approving Today's Plans
episodes.text: You return to your desk and stack the plans that passed today. You stamp the ones that meet specifications. You set the permits for construction in the outbox.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Home Organizer (pro) — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: People need things from you — questions, help, decisions. You deal with them one at a time, the way this job always does. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: Someone you're working with asks you to take on one more thing — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you today.

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Hands-on time. You make, fix or adjust the real thing in front of you — the part of the job you can touch, and the part where skill is visible. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Morning Client Talk
episodes.text: You sit down with the client at the kitchen table. You ask about budget, architectural preferences, purpose, and function. You take notes on what matters most for the interior plan.

choice.prompt: The client wants a furniture layout you know will go over budget. What do you do now?

options.label: Stay inside the budget
options.outcome: You adjust the layout to fit the budget. The client picks from lower-cost furnishings.

options.label: Show the over-budget option
options.outcome: You walk through the cost difference together. The client decides what to cut or keep.

episodes.title: Checking Safety Rules
episodes.text: You sit at your desk and open the health and safety code. You read the parts that apply to this home layout. You mark what the design must follow.

episodes.title: Planning Room Layout
episodes.text: You walk the living room with the client. You talk through space planning, layout, furnishings, and color coordination. You move two chairs to show a clearer use of space.

trial.title: Order the layout advice
items: Pick color coordination
Look at space plan
Choose furnishings or equipment
Decide layout and use
trial.explain: You start with the space plan and end with color.

episodes.title: Updating Drawings Again
episodes.text: You sit back at your computer and open the CAD file. You update the same construction documents as yesterday. You save the file and do the next sheet.

episodes.title: Blocked Doorway Problem
episodes.text: You measure the hallway and see the planned furniture blocks safe passage.

choice.prompt: The cabinet makes the path unsafe and not ADA compliant. What do you do?

options.label: Move the cabinet out
options.outcome: You redraw the plan with a clear, wide path. You update the CAD drawing to show the change.

options.label: Find a smaller cabinet
options.outcome: You look for a smaller piece that keeps the path clear. You check the new width against ADA needs.

chat.text: Can we just keep that cabinet by the door?
That leaves it too narrow for ADA access.

episodes.title: Finishing Construction Papers
episodes.text: You sit at your computer and open CAD again. You produce the updated construction documents for the safe plan. You label the layout, furnishings, and clearances.

episodes.title: Morning Instructions
episodes.text: You arrive at the house and meet your supervisor by the front door. You read the work order together to go over the rooms.

chat.text: Living room and hallway today, walls only.
Homeowner wants the trim left alone.
Start with covering, then prep.

episodes.title: Covering The Room
episodes.text: You lay dropcloths over the floors and the couch. You run masking tape and paper along the trim and windows. You press the edges down so no paint gets through.

episodes.title: Filling The Cracks
episodes.text: You walk the walls and spot cracks and small holes in the plaster. You load the caulking gun and work putty into the joints with a putty knife. One long crack by the door still looks deep.

choice.prompt: The deep crack by the door still shows after one fill. What do you do?

options.label: Give it a second fill now
options.outcome: You push in more filler and let it sit. It holds and will sand flat later.

options.label: Leave it and paint over it
options.outcome: You move on. The crack shows through the fresh paint and needs rework.

episodes.title: Sanding All Morning
episodes.text: You sand the filled spots with sandpaper. Dust hangs in the air and your arm aches. You move to the next patch and sand again, same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Rolling The Walls
episodes.text: You pour paint and roll it onto the living room walls. You keep your strokes even and overlap each pass. The color covers the old marks in two coats.

trial.title: Spot the problem
trial.scenario: You finish a section with the roller and step back. The wall looks covered except one strip where the old color shows through thin paint. The dropcloth is flat and the trim tape is still tight.
options: Thin paint spot needs another pass
Dropcloth needs moving
Trim tape needs replacing
trial.explain: The thin spot is the only uncovered paint work that needs attention.

episodes.title: Paint Where It Shouldn't
episodes.text: You are spraying near the doorway when you see the dropcloth has slipped. Bare floor shows right under your spray path.

choice.prompt: Paint is about to hit the bare floor. What do you do first?

options.label: Stop spraying and fix the dropcloth
options.outcome: You let go of the trigger and pull the cloth back over the floor. No paint reaches the wood.

options.label: Finish the pass then fix it
options.outcome: You finish the pass. Fine mist lands on the bare floor and you have to wipe it up.

episodes.title: Morning Policy Question
episodes.text: You log on at your desk. You read a message asking what the leave policy means. You pull up the written policy to explain it in plain words.

trial.title: Spot the access issue
trial.scenario: You are setting up a skill test for applicants. The test room is up stairs with no elevator noted. One applicant uses a wheelchair.
options: The test time is too early in the day
The room is not accessible under ADA rules
The test instructions are too long
trial.explain: The stairs-only room blocks equal access for the applicant.

episodes.title: Welcoming New Hire
episodes.text: You start a video call with a new hire. You walk through the hiring paperwork together.

chat.text: Hi, I am starting today. What forms do I need to sign?
I also sent my ID photo. Did you get it?
Thanks, I will stay on while I finish them.

episodes.title: Booking Test Slots
episodes.text: You sit at your calendar sending test slots. You send the same skill test link and instructions. You log each confirmation. It is the same as yesterday and the same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Explaining Benefits Choices
episodes.text: You meet online with an employee confused about benefit plans. You open the plan summary and explain the choices in plain words. She needs to pick before the deadline.

choice.prompt: She asks what to pick and wants you to choose for her. What do you do?

options.label: Explain the options again and let her decide
options.outcome: You walk through each option again. She picks one herself and you record it.

options.label: Suggest the plan most new staff pick
options.outcome: You describe what others often pick without choosing for her. She still makes her own choice.

episodes.title: Test Accommodation Problem
episodes.text: You get an urgent message before an afternoon drug test. An applicant says they need a disability accommodation for the test. The test is set to start in twenty minutes.

choice.prompt: The test time is almost here. What do you do first?

options.label: Pause the test and check the ADA rules
options.outcome: You delay the start and check what accommodation the rules allow. You reschedule the test with the change in place.

options.label: Run the test as scheduled with no change
options.outcome: You keep the original time and place. The applicant takes the test without the requested support.

options.label: Ask what support is needed and document it
options.outcome: You ask what change is needed and write it down. You use the EEO guidance to decide the next step.

episodes.title: Closing Hiring Papers
episodes.text: You open the hiring folder for today's hire. You check each signed hiring form is complete. You save the copies where they belong.

episodes.title: Reading the Plans
episodes.text: You arrive at the shop and spread the blueprints on the bench. You study the design specs for today's rooftop unit. You check where each heating component goes before you load the van.

episodes.title: Hooking Up Lines
episodes.text: You kneel beside the air handler on the job site. You connect the unit to its fuel, water, and refrigerant sources. You work slowly until it forms one complete circuit.

trial.title: Hook up the circuit
items: Connect the water source line
Check you have a complete circuit
Connect the refrigerant source line
Connect the fuel source line
trial.explain: You connect fuel, then water, then refrigerant before you check the full circuit.

episodes.title: Sweeping Clean Again
episodes.text: You stop work and sweep the work area. You coil the cords and wipe down the tools. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Listening to No Heat
episodes.text: You sit down with the homeowner at the kitchen table. You ask what the furnace has been doing.

choice.prompt: The story is still vague. What do you ask next to isolate the problem?

options.label: Ask when the cold air starts
options.outcome: You learn it blows cold right after the rattle. You go check that startup sequence next.

options.label: Ask to hear the rattle again
options.outcome: They run the furnace and you listen together. You hear exactly when the noise happens.

chat.text: It rattles and then just blows cold.
It quit last night around ten.
Did your fix this morning change anything?

episodes.title: Dead Circuit Test
episodes.text: You open the panel and find no power at the control board. You pull out your meter to test the circuit for continuity. One wire looks burnt and the reading drops out.

choice.prompt: The circuit shows no continuity on that wire. What do you do?

options.label: Lock out power and test again
options.outcome: You confirm the power is off and retest. The break in the wire stays clear on the meter.

options.label: Swap in a spare wire section
options.outcome: You shut off power and replace the burnt section. Your next test shows continuity again.

options.label: Stop and check the safety steps
options.outcome: You pause and follow the safety procedure for live panels. You keep the area clean and safe before you go on.

episodes.title: Closing Up Safe
episodes.text: You walk the job site one last time. You put tools away and clear scraps from the work area. You check that you followed all the safety procedures for the day.

episodes.title: Morning Ink Sketch
episodes.text: You arrive at your table and lay out your pens and ink. You sit down and start a loose drawing for today's piece. You test a few lines on scrap paper first.

episodes.title: Balancing Light and Space
episodes.text: You step back and look at the draft on your screen. You adjust line, space, and color to shift the mood. You try a different perspective to give the idea more room.

trial.title: Find the heavy spot
trial.scenario: You look at your illustration of a quiet street. One dark mass in the corner pulls all the attention. The rest of the space feels empty by comparison.
options: The dark mass in the corner pulls all the attention
The line work is neat and clean
The paper size is large enough
trial.explain: The heavy mass throws off the balance of the whole image.

episodes.title: Cleaning Pens Again
episodes.text: You sit and rinse the same pens and wipe the same nibs. You refill the ink and stack everything as yesterday. Same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Shaping Clay Together
episodes.text: You sit at the bench with a lump of clay and small hand tools.

choice.prompt: The clay form is still rough — what do you work on next?

options.label: Keep forming with your fingers
options.outcome: You press and smooth the shape with your fingers until the form holds.

options.label: Switch to small hand tools
options.outcome: You pick up the small tools and clean up the edges and details.

chat.text: Is this part staying thicker?
My wax keeps going soft in my hands.

episodes.title: Crack in the Carving
episodes.text: You are carving a small wood block for a three-dimensional piece. You see a thin crack open along the edge as you shape it. You stop and hold the piece still.

choice.prompt: The crack is spreading as you carve — what do you do?

options.label: Stop carving and steady it
options.outcome: You set the tool down and support the piece so the crack does not grow.

options.label: Keep shaping around it
options.outcome: You work light strokes away from the crack and reshape that side.

options.label: Switch to smoothing with abrasive
options.outcome: You rub gently with the abrasive to ease the surface and check the crack.

episodes.title: Hanging Work for Sale
episodes.text: You carry your finished artwork into the small display room. You hang each piece straight and space them along the wall. You set out the price tags for the evening sale.

episodes.title: Watching Morning Lesson
episodes.text: You arrive early and sit at the back of a classroom. You watch the teacher work through the lesson. You note what is working and what could be stronger.

trial.title: Notice What Needs Help
trial.scenario: You watch a lesson to evaluate performance. The teacher explains clearly but rushes past student questions. One teaching aid is not used the way it was designed.
options: The rushed student questions
The color of the classroom walls
The time of your next meeting
trial.explain: Student questions show where teaching skills need support.

episodes.title: Helping With Curriculum
episodes.text: You sit down with a teacher to talk through curriculum and materials.

choice.prompt: The teacher asks whether to keep using the old material or switch now.

options.label: Suggest a small switch now
options.outcome: You walk through one unit together and swap in the new material. She leaves with a clear next step to try tomorrow.

options.label: Stay with the old material
options.outcome: You agree to keep the old unit for now and review again next week. She keeps teaching as before.

chat.text: I am not sure this new material fits our unit.
Can you help me change it to match the program rules?

episodes.title: Same Materials Check
episodes.text: You sit at your desk and go through the same materials and equipment list. You check each item against yesterday's list. It is the same check you will do tomorrow.

episodes.title: Planning Afternoon Training
episodes.text: You lay out slides and handouts for a teacher training session. You plan time to show the new classroom procedure step by step. You set out the teaching aids teachers will practice with.

episodes.title: Rule Break In Class
episodes.text: You see a classroom procedure that does not follow the state education code. You pause and review the rule in your folder. You need to act before the training starts.

choice.prompt: You must decide how to handle the code violation right now.

options.label: Pause and explain the rule
options.outcome: You stop the activity and explain what the code requires. The teacher adjusts the procedure and continues the lesson.

options.label: Note it and follow up later
options.outcome: You write down what you saw and speak with the teacher after class. The activity finishes as it was.

options.label: Ask admin to step in
options.outcome: You call over the administrator to review the rule together. You all agree on a fix for next time.

episodes.title: Student Welfare Committee
episodes.text: You join a committee meeting about student welfare. You listen to other staff share concerns about learning and social needs. You agree on one small action to support students this month.

episodes.title: Morning Lead List
episodes.text: You sit down at your desk and open your list of possible clients. You send a few short messages to people you met online last week. You add two new names to call tomorrow.

episodes.title: Explaining Two Policies
episodes.text: You are on a video call with a woman choosing between two auto policies. You walk her through what each one covers and what it does not. She asks which downside should worry her more.

choice.prompt: She needs to decide and is waiting on you. What do you do?

options.label: Compare the trade-offs again plainly
options.outcome: You go over the costs and gaps side by side once more. She picks the one that fits her budget and you move on.

options.label: Suggest she take time to think
options.outcome: You send her your notes and end the call. She says she will call back after talking it over at home.

episodes.title: Renewal Records
episodes.text: You open the renewal folder and update dates and names. You click the same boxes you clicked yesterday. Tomorrow you will do it again.

episodes.title: Building Your Coverage
episodes.text: You sit with a new customer's notes for home and auto needs. You pull coverages together into one program that fits him. You read it back to check nothing is missing.

trial.title: Put Coverage Together
items: Write the choices into one program
Ask what risks they need covered
Check it fits the person
Pick coverages to match those needs
trial.explain: You learn the needs first, then match coverages before writing it up.

episodes.title: Renewal About To Lapse
episodes.text: Your screen flags a property policy that ends today and the client just joined the chat.

choice.prompt: The renewal closes in an hour. What do you do first?

options.label: Process the renewal now
options.outcome: You renew the policy and send the confirmation. He stays covered without a gap.

options.label: Explain the lapse risk first
options.outcome: You explain he could be uncovered tonight if it is not renewed. He asks you to renew it right away.

options.label: Offer to review other options first
options.outcome: You start comparing other property policies with him. The clock keeps running on today's deadline.

chat.text: I forgot about the renewal. Does this mean I have no cover tonight?
I can pay now if that keeps it going.

episodes.title: Filing Today's Sales
episodes.text: You log today's sold policies for auto and life into the record. You save the renewal confirmations with the right files. You close the folders when everything lines up.

episodes.title: Opening Claim Files
episodes.text: You arrive at your desk and open the overnight claims queue. You pull the forms and attached records for a water damage claim. You read line by line to see what coverage applies.

episodes.title: Same Queue Again
episodes.text: You sit down to pay and process the small clear claims under your limit. You click through the same screens you used yesterday. You approve, you code, you move to the next one. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Explaining the Denial
episodes.text: You sit with a policyholder who is waiting for an answer on her claim. You walk through what the records show.

choice.prompt: She asks you to approve it even though the records do not show coverage. What do you do?

options.label: Hold to what you found
options.outcome: You explain the coverage decision kindly and show her what the records say. She is upset but leaves with the written reason.

options.label: Offer to re-check the records
options.outcome: You pull the file again with her and go over each page together. You still reach the same decision, but she sees the steps.

chat.text: Can you just tell me straight — am I covered?
I sent everything you asked for. I need this settled.
Can't you just approve it anyway?

episodes.title: Checking the Numbers
episodes.text: You pull the repair bills and statements for a car claim. You verify each number and compare them to company procedures. You mark what is valid before any settlement moves forward.

trial.title: Check coverage in order
items: Note whether coverage applies
Open the claim forms
Read the supporting records
Compare details to the policy coverage
trial.explain: You open and read the file first, then you decide on coverage last.

episodes.title: Angry Call Waiting
episodes.text: You get a call about a claim you were about to settle — the damage is worse than reported. The caller is upset and wants payment today. You have to keep things fair while moving fast.

choice.prompt: The caller presses you to settle right now for the higher amount. What do you do?

options.label: Pause and investigate the new damage
options.outcome: You tell him you need to check the new facts first. The settlement waits a day while you confirm what is valid.

options.label: Settle only what you have verified
options.outcome: You pay the part you have already checked and leave the new amount open. He gets something today and the rest stays under review.

episodes.title: Writing Up Findings
episodes.text: You sit down to write up your investigation notes from today. You list what you gathered and what you recommend. You file the report so the file shows your reasoning.

episodes.title: Morning Application File
episodes.text: You arrive at your desk and open the first application folder. You read through health forms and financial statements. You note the property value and its current condition.

choice.prompt: The health history looks unclear and the property value is high. What do you do next?

options.label: Ask for more health details before deciding
options.outcome: You set the file aside and request the missing records. The file waits until the information arrives.

options.label: Continue your risk review with what you have
options.outcome: You keep reading and mark what is still uncertain. You note the gaps you need to close later.

episodes.title: Checking Existing Coverage
episodes.text: You sit down with the company records. You look up how much insurance is already in force on this risk. You check related risks and write down the totals. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Waiting On Medical Details
episodes.text: You need more information before you can finish the file. You message the field office to ask for it.

chat.text: Got your note about the application.
Do you need the full medical report or just the recent visit?
Just ask them for the recent visit and the quoted rate sheet.

episodes.title: Storm Exposure Review
episodes.text: You return after lunch and pull the group of related properties. You think about losses if a storm hits them all at once. You compare the total insurance to what a catastrophe could cost.

trial.title: Spot the main worry
trial.scenario: You review three risks close together on the coast. Two carry small policies. One carries a very large policy in a storm area.
options: The very large policy in the storm area
The two small policies inland
The color of the application folder
trial.explain: The large coastal policy creates the biggest possible loss from one storm.

episodes.title: Too Much Risk
episodes.text: You look again at an application with serious health issues and a damaged property. The degree of risk is well past what the company allows. You prepare to decline the excessive risk.

choice.prompt: The file is clearly over the limit. How do you handle it?

options.label: Decline the risk now
options.outcome: You mark the file declined and close it. The applicant is not offered coverage.

options.label: Hold it one more day for another look
options.outcome: You leave the file open until tomorrow. You recheck the same papers with no new information.

options.label: Send it back for a second medical opinion
options.outcome: You write for more medical input and wait. The final decision stays on hold.

episodes.title: Explaining The Decision
episodes.text: You sit down to write to the field representative. You explain the underwriting policy in plain terms. You quote the rate rules and close the file for the day.

episodes.title: Meeting About Budget
episodes.text: You sit down with the client at their dining table. You ask about budget, purpose, and what they like. You take notes on how they want to use the rooms.

choice.prompt: The client wants a larger layout than the budget allows. What do you do first?

options.label: Show what the current budget covers
options.outcome: You walk through what fits now. The client picks what matters most.

options.label: Ask which function matters most
options.outcome: You list the rooms by daily use. The client chooses where to put the money.

episodes.title: Checking Safety Codes
episodes.text: You are back at your desk with the code book open. You look up health and safety requirements for the remodel. You mark what affects your plan.

trial.title: Spot the safety issue
trial.scenario: You review a small office plan. The hallway looks clear and the lights look fine. One exit path is blocked by a storage cabinet.
options: Hallway paint color
Blocked exit path
Desk layout style
trial.explain: A blocked exit path breaks health and safety requirements.

episodes.title: Talking Through Layout
episodes.text: You meet the client in the living room. You suggest a layout and show where the furnishings could go. You hold up color samples next to the light.

episodes.title: Updating Construction Drawings
episodes.text: You sit at your computer and open CAD. You move the same lines and labels you moved yesterday. Tomorrow you will do it again.

episodes.title: Doorway Too Narrow
episodes.text: You measure the hallway doorway on site. It is too narrow to be safe and ADA compliant.

choice.prompt: The doorway fails ADA width. How do you handle it now?

options.label: Redraw the plan wider
options.outcome: You widen the doorway in the plan. You send the update for review.

options.label: Pause and check the code again
options.outcome: You recheck the ADA width rule. You confirm the fix before you redraw.

options.label: Call the client about the change
options.outcome: You explain why the doorway must change. The client agrees to the wider opening.

chat.text: That doorway width will not pass. What are we doing?
We can widen it six inches if the client agrees.

episodes.title: Finishing Today's Documents
episodes.text: You sit back at your computer. You finish the construction documents in CAD. You save the sheets and close the files.

episodes.title: Checking Morning Systems
episodes.text: You arrive at your desk and log in. You open the system monitor and look through the daily performance of the computers. Everything looks steady as you note what is running.

trial.title: Order a new setup
items: Install the operating system
Plug in the cables
Install the needed software
Confirm it starts for the new user
trial.explain: You connect the cables first, then the system and software, then confirm it works.

episodes.title: First Help Request
episodes.text: You see a new message from a coworker whose software will not open.

choice.prompt: The spreadsheet keeps freezing. What do you do first?

options.label: Ask what changed and walk through it together
options.outcome: You ask what they clicked and when it froze. You stay with them and work toward an answer.

options.label: Ask them to restart and try again
options.outcome: They restart and try to open the file again. You wait to see if the problem clears.

chat.text: Morning, my spreadsheet keeps freezing when I try to open it.
I need it for a meeting soon. Can you help?

episodes.title: Same Questions Again
episodes.text: You answer another message about how to use the software. It is the same kind of question as yesterday. You give the same steps and move to the next message.

episodes.title: Setting Up Laptop
episodes.text: You sit down with a laptop for a new employee. You plug in the cables and install the operating system. You add the needed software and check that it starts.

episodes.title: Computer Will Not Start
episodes.text: You get an urgent note that a computer will not start at all. You go over and run a quick diagnostic. You pull up the technical manual to check the next step.

choice.prompt: The diagnostic points to a loose part but you are not sure. What now?

options.label: Check the manual and reseat the part
options.outcome: You follow the manual steps and refit the part. You test the machine to see if it starts.

options.label: Confer with the user about what happened
options.outcome: You ask the user what happened before it failed. You use their answer to guide your next check.

options.label: Escalate and mark the machine down
options.outcome: You leave the machine off and note the problem. You tell the user you will follow up.

episodes.title: Fixing Office Printer
episodes.text: You walk to the printer that keeps jamming. You check the installation and fit a small replacement part. You run a test page and it prints clean.

episodes.title: Cutting Morning Rings
episodes.text: You arrive at your bench and pick up yesterday's marked blanks. You cut small rings and brooches to size, then file the edges with hand files.

episodes.title: Smoothing Soldered Joints
episodes.text: You sit down with a tray of soldered bracelets. You work each joint smooth and even before polishing.

trial.title: Smooth a soldered joint
items: Polish the smoothed area with a polishing wheel
Smooth the area with emery paper
Check the smoothed spot
File the soldered joint with a hand file
trial.explain: You file first, then smooth with emery paper, then polish, then check.

episodes.title: Polishing Batch Pieces
episodes.text: You load lockets and bracelets through the same polish and rinse. You do the same motions you did yesterday. Same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Setting Gold Stones
episodes.text: You sit back down to make a small order in gold and silver with stones. You fit the stones into the mounts you cut this morning.

choice.prompt: One mount feels a little tight for the stone. What do you do?

options.label: Ease the seat a bit more
options.outcome: You file a little more and the stone seats flat. It takes ten extra minutes.

options.label: Press the stone in now
options.outcome: You press it in and the edge catches. You have to lift it back out and fix the seat.

episodes.title: Catching a Flaw
episodes.text: You hold a finished ring under the magnifying glass to check it. You see a rough spot still showing near the joint.

choice.prompt: The piece is due to leave today. What do you do?

options.label: Fix it now at the bench
options.outcome: You re-file, smooth, and buff the spot, then check it again. The piece ships a little late but clean.

options.label: Set it aside for rework
options.outcome: You tag the spot and put it back in the rework tray. You pick up the next piece to check.

episodes.title: Final Polish Check
episodes.text: You give the day's finished pieces a last clean and polish. You look them over with the loupe and measuring tool to check the specs.

episodes.title: Morning Work Orders
episodes.text: You arrive at the lot. You read the work orders for the day. You note what to pick up and what gear you will need.

episodes.title: Checking Storage Area
episodes.text: You walk through the equipment storage area. You straighten the stacks and check that everything is covered and dry. It looks the same as yesterday and will look the same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Sorting the Pile
episodes.text: You stand by the pile at the curb. You sort chairs, wood, and bagged trash into separate groups. You keep what loads first closest to the truck.

trial.title: Sort Before You Load
items: Load the sorted groups onto the truck
Look at what has to move first
Sort the cargo into separate piles
Unload the groups at the drop-off
trial.explain: You check first, then sort, then load and unload in that order.

episodes.title: Marking Each Container
episodes.text: You stand by the filled containers with tags in hand. Your colleague wants them marked clearly before the run.

choice.prompt: One tag smudges as you write. What do you do?

options.label: Rewrite it on a fresh tag
options.outcome: You write a new tag and tie it on tight. The load stays easy to tell apart.

options.label: Leave it and load it anyway
options.outcome: You load the smudged tag as is. You have to open the container later to check what is inside.

chat.text: Which one has the garage wood?
Can you tag it so we don't mix it up?
Just write it big on the tag.

episodes.title: Straps Come Loose
episodes.text: You pull over and check the back. A couch has shifted and a strap hangs loose. The padding has slipped off the corner.

choice.prompt: The load is shifting. What do you fix first?

options.label: Reset the bracing and straps now
options.outcome: You reset the bracing and pull the straps tight. The couch holds steady for the rest of the drive.

options.label: Keep driving and fix it later
options.outcome: You drive on with the loose strap. The couch rubs hard against the rail and gets gouged.

episodes.title: Putting Gear Away
episodes.text: You back into the yard at the end of the run. You carry the padding and straps back to storage. You set everything in its place so it stays dry and protected.

episodes.title: Calibrating Morning Machines
episodes.text: You arrive and pull on your gloves. You set up the analyzer and run the calibration checks. You clean the bench and test the equipment for sterility.

episodes.title: Crossmatch Blood Counts
episodes.text: You sit down with today's transfusion requests. You run blood counts and check compatibility for transfusion. One sample looks a little off on the first run.

choice.prompt: The count is borderline and the ward is waiting. What do you do?

options.label: Rerun the count
options.outcome: You rerun the same sample. You get a clearer number to record for the transfusion check.

options.label: Ask a senior to review
options.outcome: You hold the sample and hand the printout to the senior. You wait while they check the result with you.

episodes.title: Same Urine Chemistry Line
episodes.text: You load the next rack of blood and urine tubes. You run them through the automatic analyzer the same way as yesterday. You watch the numbers come out and keep feeding samples.

episodes.title: Plating Morning Swabs
episodes.text: You collect the labeled specimens from the tray. You streak them onto plates to grow and isolate what is there. You sit them in the incubator for later identification.

trial.title: Order the culture steps
items: Isolate the microorganisms
Cultivate the sample
Identify the microorganism
Obtain the specimen
trial.explain: You always obtain the specimen first, then grow it, isolate it, and identify it last.

episodes.title: Control Fails Specification
episodes.text: You are checking test results against specification when the control fails.

choice.prompt: The result does not meet specification. What do you do first?

options.label: Stop and recheck the device
options.outcome: You stop reporting and recheck the device and controls. You find whether the error is in the run or the sample.

options.label: Repeat the test sample
options.outcome: You run the patient sample again on the same device. You compare both runs before deciding anything.

chat.text: My control is high too. Did yours fail?
Hold all reporting. Recheck the device and the controls.

episodes.title: Entering Today's Findings
episodes.text: You sit at the computer with the day's slips. You enter the blood and urine findings from the microscope and analyzer. You double-check each entry matches the label.

episodes.title: Pulling the old records
episodes.text: You arrive at the office and open the file for today's parcel. You search legal records, survey records, and land titles for anything about these boundaries. You stack the deeds and old plats you will carry outside.

trial.title: Order the record search
items: Note the boundary lines to check outside
Pull the deeds and titles for the parcel
File what you found with the job folder
Look up older surveys for the same area
trial.explain: You pull the deeds first, then check old surveys before noting what to verify.

episodes.title: Walking the boundary line
episodes.text: You drive out and set up where the deed says the corner should be. You direct the survey to establish the legal boundary for the property. You work the line point to point off the deed.

episodes.title: Checking your numbers
episodes.text: You sit on the tailgate and run through the measurements again. You verify the accuracy of the survey data and calculations from this morning. You mark one distance to re-shoot after lunch.

episodes.title: Logging the same points
episodes.text: You are back on the instrument logging the same kind of shots. You record each measurement and check the math the same way. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Talking through the line
episodes.text: The owner meets you by the fence and asks where the line really runs.

choice.prompt: The owner wants you to agree the fence is the legal line. What do you do?

options.label: Point to the deed calls
options.outcome: You walk him through what the deed and old survey say. He listens and lets you finish the line.

options.label: Say you will check again
options.outcome: You recheck the corner and show him the same result. The talk ends and you get back to work.

chat.text: My deed says it goes to that oak, right?
Show him what the deed calls say.
So you are saying the fence is off?

episodes.title: When nothing lines up
episodes.text: You compare today's measurements to the legal description and they do not close. You check your calculations twice and the gap is still there. You need to decide before you write anything up.

choice.prompt: Your survey data does not match the deed description. What do you do first?

options.label: Hold the map and re-verify
options.outcome: You do not certify the survey yet. You plan a recheck of the records and field measurements tomorrow.

options.label: Write the description anyway
options.outcome: You catch yourself and stop. You leave the legal description unwritten until the numbers are verified.

options.label: Note it in the report
options.outcome: You write down the mismatch and what you checked. The office has a clear record of the problem.

episodes.title: Reading The Land
episodes.text: You arrive at your desk and open the folder for a new backyard project. You look at notes on site location, drainage, and where the house sits. You mark the wet low spot that will shape the plan.

episodes.title: Talking Through Plans
episodes.text: You sit down with the client and the architect at a small table. You go over the early sketch and how it fits the house and yard. You listen while they point at the patio and the slope.

choice.prompt: The architect wants to shift the patio closer to the wet low area. What do you do?

options.label: Keep it where it drains well
options.outcome: You keep the patio on higher ground. The architect redraws the edge and you move on.

options.label: Agree to move it lower
options.outcome: You move the patio on the sketch. You note you will need to recheck drainage before it is final.

episodes.title: Working Around Trees
episodes.text: You walk the yard with your notebook. You find two old oaks and a rock edge worth keeping. You bend the path on your sketch to wind around them.

trial.title: Spot The Problem
trial.scenario: You walk the side yard after rain. Water pools near the house foundation. An old oak stands healthy on high ground nearby.
options: Pooled water by the foundation
Healthy oak on high ground
Dry path by the fence
trial.explain: Standing water by a structure means drainage needs attention first.

episodes.title: Updating Cost Sheets
episodes.text: You sit back down and open the cost estimate sheet. You type in the same plant and paving prices as yesterday. You will do the same again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Wall Out Of Line
episodes.text: You arrive on site to check the new retaining wall. It does not match the line on your plan.

choice.prompt: The wall is two feet off your spec to miss roots. What do you tell the crew?

options.label: Stop and hold the work
options.outcome: You ask the crew to stop on the wall. You check the new line against drainage and the plan.

options.label: Let them keep building
options.outcome: You let the crew keep laying block. You note the change and check how it affects the rest of the plan.

options.label: Redraw the line now
options.outcome: You mark a new line that clears the roots and meets the spec. The crew waits while you confirm it.

chat.text: We set the wall two feet over to miss the roots.
Should we keep building from here?
Can you tell us if this still works?

episodes.title: Drawing The Plan
episodes.text: You are back at your desk. You clean up the site plan and write out the specs. You save the file for the client and the builder.
